Cave Crawl

Torchlight, a loose pebble, and two explorers hiding in the dark.

KidsEasy
Game code
KO-03
Players
1 to 4
Time
10 to 15 min
Age
5+
Dice
1 die
Pawns
Explorer

Times include about 20% for learning the rules and for thinking. The raw simulated lengths are in the stats for nerds.

The whole game in one line

Find twins in a face-down cave. Your die says how far you can reach.

What you need

Twin pairs
6, 8 or 12 pairs from the deck
1 die
your reach
1 pawn each
your explorer

Fronts of the cards are private, backs are public. Reference cards are the seven small cards in the box (Ref 1 to 7).

Set up

  • Take a card, find its twin (same child, same name), and put both aside. Repeat for 6 pairs (L1), 8 (L2) or 12 (L3).
  • Shuffle those cards. Lay them face down in a grid: 3×4, 4×4 or 6×4.
  • Stand your pawn on a card in the middle. Youngest starts.

How to play

On your turn:

  1. Roll the die. That number is your reach in steps.

  2. Flip any two face-down cards within reach. A step is one move up, down, left or right. Empty spaces count.

  3. Twins? Keep both and say the name. Not twins? Turn them back face down.

  4. Move your pawn to the space of the second card you flipped.

  5. Fewer than two cards in reach? Put your pawn on any space. Your turn ends.

How it ends

When every pair has been taken, most pairs wins. Tie: share the win.

Words in this game

  • Twins the same child, so the same face and name. Their numbers add to 9.
  • Reach the most steps from your pawn that a card may be.

Common questions

  • Can I flip a card that is further than my reach? No. Both cards must be within your reach.

  • Must the two cards be next to each other? No. They only each have to be within your reach from your pawn.

  • Everyone sees my flips. Is that right? Yes. Memory is the whole game.

  • The last two cards are too far apart. What now? Put your pawn anywhere on your turn. Reach is measured from the new space next time.

Tips

  • Remember what you see, but say the name or place out loud. Perfect memory beats a player who remembers only the last 4 turns 69% of the time at L2 and 84% at L3, and saying it helps you store it.

  • Use your move to set up the next turn. The pawn ends on your second card, so flip a first card you do not need and a second that puts the pawn near the cards you want next.

  • When the reach die is low, flip cards near the pawn that you already know are not twins, to move the pawn safely rather than waste a flip.

  • At L3 say the number the twin must have (9 minus the first card) before you flip the second. It forces you to search your memory rather than guess.

  • With a 5-year-old, start at L1 with a 3 by 4 cave of 6 pairs and let the child flip while you say the name. If they cannot remember, point to where a card was.

Worked example

The cards below are the real cards from your deck.

  1. L2. A rolls 4. A flips Kanasu (3) and Kanasu (6). Same face, so A keeps both and says 'Kanasu!' A checks the bond: 3 + 6 = 9.

  2. B rolls 2. B flips Pinku and Nakul. They are not twins, so both go back down. Everyone saw them, so everyone can use that.

Level ladder

L1 · age 5

3×4 cave, 6 pairs. Say the name of each pair you keep.

L2 · ages 6 to 7

4×4 cave, 8 pairs. Say the place on each card you flip, to help you remember.

L3 · age 8 and up

6×4 cave, 12 pairs. Before you flip the second card, say the number its twin must have (9 minus the first). Act out both expressions for 1 bonus point.

Solo

Clear the cave alone, counting turns. L1: Gold 11 or fewer, Silver 13, Bronze 15. L2: 16, 18, 21. L3: 28, 32, 38.

Two players

Two players work as written. Every flip is public, so memory is the skill.

Maths in this game

Distance in steps, bonds to 9 on every pair, and memory. L3 asks for the missing number before the flip.

Which card elements do the work

Serial 1 to 54Not used
Letter tileNot used
People and namesRule twins by face, say the name
ExpressionRule act both (L3)
PlaceFlavour the two places differ, so only the face matches
TeamNot used

Stats for nerds: what the simulations showed

Lengths in this section are raw simulated times, without the learning and thinking allowance.

  • Solo turns with perfect memory: L1 median 11 (90% within 13), L2 median 15 (within 18), L3 median 25 (within 31). Remembering only the last 6 turns: L2 median 16, L3 median 30.
  • The reach die costs about 3 extra turns over unlimited reach.
  • A stall can happen when two remaining cards sit too far apart to reach together. That is why a player with fewer than two cards in reach may hop the pawn to any space.
  • Skill: a player with perfect memory beats a player who remembers 4 turns 69% of the time at L2 and 84% at L3. Four equal players each win 25%.
  • Length: all players' turns together equal about the solo count, so L1 about 11 turns (4 minutes), L2 about 16 (6 minutes), L3 about 30 (10 minutes).

Llama Trek

The llamas are climbing the trail one step at a time. Who can unload their pack first?

Inspired by L.A.M.A. by Reiner Knizia, with dice twists at L3

RecommendedKidsFamilyEasy
Game code
KO-04
Players
2 to 5
Time
10 to 15 min
Age
5+
Dice
None at L1 · 1 die from L2 (Suit key)
Pawns
None

Times include about 20% for learning the rules and for thinking. The raw simulated lengths are in the stats for nerds.

The whole game in one line

Lay cards on the trail one after another to empty your hand first. Whatever you hold when someone finishes costs you points.

What you need

All 54 cardsdeal 6 each, the rest is the draw pile
1 dieL2 and up · wild suit, read on the Suit key
REF 4the Suit key (other side)
Pencil and paperto add up points

Fronts of the cards are private, backs are public. Reference cards are the seven small cards in the box (Ref 1 to 7).

Set up

  • Shuffle all 54 cards. Deal 6 cards to each player. Look at yours. Keep them secret.

  • Turn the next card face up. This is the trail. Put the rest face down as the draw pile.

  • L2 and up: roll the die and read it on the Suit key (Ref 4). That suit number is the wild suit for this round.

  • Youngest starts. Each new round, the start passes to the left.

How to play

On your turn:

  1. Look at the top card of the trail. Is there a card in your hand you can lay on it? L1: it has the same number, or it shares a border colour with the top card. L2 and up: it has the same number, or the number one higher (a 9 goes on to a 1), or the two numbers add to 9, or it shows the wild suit on one of its medals.

  2. If you can lay a card, you must. Pick one and put it on the trail. It is the new top card.

  3. If you cannot, draw 1 card from the pile. If you can lay it, lay it. If not, keep it. Then your turn ends.

  4. L3 only, after you lay a card from your hand: roll the die for the Twist. 1 = the trail turns round, play goes the other way. 2 = the next player misses a turn. 3 = the next player draws 1 card. 4 = you name a colour: the next player must lay a card with that colour or draw. 5 or 6 = nothing.

  5. L3 only, instead of your turn you may fold, once a round. You are out of this round and score only your single biggest number.

How it ends

The round ends the moment someone lays their last card (at L1, finish the turn round so everyone has had the same number of turns). That player scores 0. Everyone else adds up the numbers of the cards left in their hand. After all rounds, the lowest total wins. Rounds: 3 with 2 players, or 2 with 3 to 5 players (L2 with 3 players: 3 rounds). Ties share the win.

Words in this game

  • Trail the pile of cards you lay on. Only the top card counts.
  • Wild suit the suit number you rolled at the start of the round. Any card with that suit on one of its medals can go on any top card.
  • One higher the next number up. 4 goes on 3. A 9 goes on to a 1.
  • Bond two numbers that add to 9, like 3 and 6, or 1 and 8.
  • Twist the L3 die roll after you lay a card.

Common questions

  • Can I choose not to play a card I can play? No. If you can lay a card, you must. You choose which one.

  • What if the draw pile runs out? Keep the top card of the trail. Shuffle the rest of the trail and use it as the new draw pile.

  • Does a card with the same number as the top have to match a colour too? No. At L1 either one is enough: the same number or a shared colour. At L2 and up colours do not matter at all.

  • If I draw a card I can lay, can I roll the Twist? No. Only a card laid from your hand gets a Twist roll.

  • Can the same card fit in more than one way? Yes. A 5 fits on a 4 as one higher and also as a bond to 9. It only has to fit one way.

Tips

  • Lay your biggest legal number first. The smart bot always did, because the numbers left in your hand cost you points when someone else goes out.

  • Check every way a card fits: same number, one higher (a 9 goes on a 1), a bond to 9, or the wild suit. A 5 fits a 4 and also a 4 as a bond, so use the fit that keeps a better card for later.

  • Hold the wild suit cards back. They can go on any top card, so keep them for when nothing else fits rather than using them early.

  • At L3 fold when your hand is full of 8s and 9s. Folding scores only your biggest number, and it added about 9 points of win share for the better player at 2 players.

  • With a 5-year-old, use L1 and finish the turn round, then count the hand together. Adding the leftover cards is the maths practice, so do it slowly.

Worked example

L2, two players, wild suit 1 (the first suit on the Suit key). All cards are real cards from the deck.

  1. The trail card is Bn Sharada (2), number 2. The die shows 1, so the wild suit is 1. A goes first.

  2. A holds Ammlu (2), Kanasu (3), Dharsh (7), Sharada (6) and Avika (5). Ammlu (2) is a 2, the same number. Kanasu (3) is a 3, one higher. Dharsh (7) is a 7, and 2 + 7 = 9, a bond. Sharada (6) shows suit 1, the wild suit. Avika (5) is a 5: not a 2 or 3, 2 + 5 is not 9, no suit 1. So four cards can go and one cannot. A lays Dharsh (7), the biggest number, to get rid of 7 points. The trail is now a 7.

  3. Say B has nothing that fits, so B draws one card from the pile. It is Nysha (8), an 8: one higher than 7. B lays it. The trail is now an 8.

  4. A cannot lay a 2, 3 or 5 on an 8 by number, but Sharada (6) shows the wild suit 1, so A lays it. The trail is now a 6. A has Ammlu (2), Kanasu (3) and Avika (5) left, which add to 10 points if B finishes first.

Level ladder

L1 · age 5

Age 5. No die. A card goes on if it has the same number or shares a border colour with the top card. Finish the turn round so everyone has had the same number of turns. Ties share the win.

L2 · ages 6 to 7

Ages 6 to 7. Roll the wild suit. Cards go on by same number, one higher (9 to 1), bond to 9, or wild suit. Adding up the cards left in your hand is the maths.

L3 · age 8 and up

Age 8 and up. The same as L2, plus the Twist die after each card you lay (reverse, miss a turn, draw 1, name a colour) and the right to fold once a round and score only your biggest card.

Solo

Play one round alone with a hand of 6 and a new trail card. Count your turns until your hand is empty. Fewer is better. If you draw twice in a row and cannot lay either card, turn up a new top card for the trail. L3 solo: the Twist die only matters on a 3: draw 1. Medals, L1: Bronze 10 turns, Silver 7, Gold 6. L2: Bronze 26, Silver 15, Gold 8. L3: Bronze 31, Silver 18, Gold 10.

Two players

As written: 3 rounds. At L1 the first player to empty their hand scores 0; the other adds the numbers left. A friendly two-player game, and the Twist reverse does nothing except change who plays next.

Maths and skills in this game

Comparing numbers, counting on one, number bonds to 9, and adding up leftovers. At L3 deciding whether to fold is about estimating a total.

Variants and options

  • The L3 Twist die and fold bring in a twist-die variant (hand of 7, play on the top card by colour, suit or bond). Colour matching is kept at L1 and in the Twist 4 colour call.

Which card elements do the work

NumberRule same number, one higher or a bond to 9 decides which cards go on, and the leftovers are your score
ColoursRule at L1 a shared border colour lets a card go on; at L3 the Twist 4 names a colour
Suit pairRule at L2 and up the wild suit is the suit on either medal
Back patternNot used
TeamNot used
Letter tileNot used
SerialNot used
NamesFlavour say the child's name as you lay the card
ExpressionNot used
PlaceNot used

Stats for nerds: what the simulations showed

Lengths in this section are raw simulated times, without the learning and thinking allowance.

Status: Simulated. L2: smart beats random 57% at 2p (50% even), 33% at 4p (25% even); median 9 to 11 min; 0 stalls

SettingResult
2p L2 (3 rounds)smart 57%, median 58 turns (about 9.7 min), ties 2%
3p L2 (3 rounds)smart 46% (33% even), 11.3 min
4p L2 (2 rounds)smart 33% (25% even), 8.7 min
5p L2 (2 rounds)smart 29% (20% even), 10.2 min
2p L3smart 69%, 10.5 min
4p L3smart 35%, 11 min
4p L1ties 49%, spread 25/25/24/25, 8 min
Solo L2median 15 turns, gold 8, silver 15, bronze 26

  • Bots on the real 54 cards, 2,000 games per setting: a smart bot (always lays its biggest legal number) against random players.

  • Adding the wild suit cut rounds sharply: with only same number, one higher and bond, a round took a median 55 turns with two random players and 43 with four, against 17 and 25 with the wild suit, which is why the wild suit die is part of L2 and L3. No round stalled in 2,000 games per setting, and the longest was 101 turns.

  • L1 (same number or shared colour) takes about 12 turns a round with two players. Without a finish-the-round rule the first player in each round almost always empties first (four players split 28%, 41%, 20% and 12% by seat); finishing the turn round the table gives 25%, 25%, 23% and 26%, at the price of ties: 10% of two-player games, 36% with three, 49% with four and 61% with five (ties share the win).

  • L2: the smart bot wins 57% with two players (50% is even), 46% with three (33%), 33% with four (25%) and 29% with five (20%). Skill counts but luck decides most games. Equal bots split the wins within a point or two of fair, with ties of 2% to 7%.

  • L3 (Twist and fold): the smart bot wins 69% with two players (59% with the Twist alone), 42% with three, 35% with four and 30% with five. The fold is a real choice: it adds about 9 points of win share for the better player at two players.

  • Length at 10 seconds per turn, using the chosen rounds: L1 6 to 10 min, L2 about 9 to 11 min, L3 about 9 to 13 min. A median L2 two-player game was 58 turns (3 rounds), L3 63 turns.

  • Scores (leftover totals over the rounds): L2 median 15 with two players (middle half 6 to 24), 20 with three over 3 rounds, 15 to 16 with four and five over 2 rounds.

  • Solo bots (3,000 to 4,000 runs): L1 median 6 turns; L2 median 15 (25% in 8 or fewer, 75% in 26 or fewer, 90% in 40); L3 median 18. Without the new-trail-card rule L2 ran to a worst case of 205 turns and a 90th percentile of 53; with it, 129 and 40.

Not tested:

  • Not tested: real children's timing, or whether they remember the three L2 matches. The 10 second turn is an assumption.

  • Not tested: human choice for the Twist 4 colour. The bot names its own commonest colour, and a human may do better.

  • Not tested: fold thresholds other than one simple rule (hand total at least 22 and an opponent at 2 cards or fewer).

Rule card text

Text for the printed card (63.5 x 88.9 mm). Layout comes later.

Front

LLAMA TREK. The llamas climb the trail. Empty your pack first. Deal 6 each. Turn up one card: the trail. Roll the die on the Suit key (L2 up): that is the wild suit. On your turn, lay a card on the trail if it has the same number, one higher (9 then 1), a number that adds to 9 with it, or the wild suit. You must lay if you can. Cannot? Draw 1 and lay it if it fits. First to lay their last card scores 0. Everyone else adds up what they hold. Lowest total wins.

Back

LEVELS. L1: same number or shared border colour only. Finish the turn round. L2: same number, one higher, bond to 9, or wild suit. L3: after you lay a card roll the Twist. 1 turn round. 2 next player misses a turn. 3 next player draws 1. 4 name a colour, next player lays it or draws. 5 or 6 nothing. Fold once a round: you score only your biggest card. ROUNDS: 3 with 2 players, 2 with 3 to 5. SOLO turns to empty 6 cards. L2 Gold 8, Silver 15, Bronze 26. L3 Gold 10, Silver 18, Bronze 31.

Camp Kitchen

Hungry guests arrive at the camp kitchen. The cook can only reach part of the buffet at a time.

Inspired by Point Salad (take two from the market)

RecommendedKidsEasy
Game code
KO-05
Players
1 to 4
Time
10 to 15 min
Age
5+
Dice
1 die at L1 · 2 dice at L2 and L3 (1 die for the Mode bonus)
Pawns
Cook (1 pawn)

Times include about 20% for learning the rules and for thinking. The raw simulated lengths are in the stats for nerds.

The whole game in one line

Lay out a 3 by 3 buffet. Take two cards from the cook's column or the next one, and the cook moves there. Make your plate add up to the guest's appetite. First to 4 stars wins.

What you need

All 54 cards9 on the buffet, the rest a draw pile
1 or 2 dicethe guest's appetite (Modes: one die for the bonus, Suit key or Team key, Ref 4)
1 pawnthe cook
Pencil and paperRainbow and Photo modes, to count points

Fronts of the cards are private, backs are public. Reference cards are the seven small cards in the box (Ref 1 to 7).

Set up

  • Shuffle. Lay 9 cards face up in a 3 by 3 buffet (3 columns of 3). Keep the rest face down as the draw pile.

  • Stand the pawn (the cook) at the foot of the middle column.

  • Everyone starts with an empty plate. Your plate is held in your hand, up to 5 cards, secret.

  • Roll for the first guest's appetite. Youngest starts.

How to play

On your turn:

  1. Choose the cook's column or the column to its right. The right edge wraps round to the left. Take any 2 cards from that column onto your plate.

  2. Move the cook to the column you took from. Fill the gap from the draw pile.

  3. Serve? If cards on your plate add up exactly to the guest's appetite, put them down and take a star. Roll a new guest. L1: 1, 2 or 3 cards. L2 and L3: 2 or 3 cards.

  4. Keep at most 5 cards on your plate. Throw the extras face up on a discard pile.

  5. If nobody serves for a whole round, the guest leaves hungry: roll a new one.

  6. L1: the appetite is one die (1 to 6). L2: two dice added (2 to 12). L3: two dice, and you may serve either their sum or their difference.

How it ends

First to 4 stars wins at once. If the draw pile runs out the game ends: most stars wins. Tie: fewer cards on your plate. Modes: Rainbow Camp and Expedition Photo use the same take-two turn but end when the draw pile is empty (Rainbow) or when every photo is full (Photo); see the Modes in the variants list.

Words in this game

  • Appetite The number the guest wants. Your cards must add up to it exactly.
  • Cook The pawn. It decides which columns you can reach.
  • Plate The cards in your hand, up to 5.
  • Mode A different way to score the same take-two game: Rainbow Camp or Expedition Photo.

Common questions

  • Can I take one card from each of two columns? No. Both cards come from the same column.

  • Which way does the cook move? To the column you took from. That is where it stood or the one to its right. The right edge wraps to the left.

  • Why not just take what I need? You can. But the cook moves, and the next player can only reach the cook's column and the one to its right. Leave the cards they need out of reach.

  • What if my plate goes over 5? Throw away down to 5, face up. Everyone can see what you threw, so you cannot hide what you are collecting.

  • What does the difference mean at L3? Dice 5 and 3 give an appetite of 8 (added) or 2 (5 minus 3). Serve either.

Tips

  • Look at the cook before you take. The next player can reach only the cook's column and the one to its right, so take from a column that moves the cook away from the cards you are collecting.

  • Leave the next player nothing they can serve. The look-ahead bot, which avoids leaving a serve, beat random players 89%, 83% and 72% at 2, 3 and 4 players.

  • Keep a flexible plate. Cards you throw over 5 are shown face up, so everyone sees what you gave up, and a mix of small and middle numbers can make many appetites.

  • At L3 remember the difference counts: dice 5 and 3 mean 8 or 2. Check both targets before you take, because one plate can serve twice as often.

  • With a 5-year-old, play L1 and do the adding together out loud: 'We need 4. You have a 3. What do we need?' The one-die appetite is 1 to 6, so there is always a small sum to find.

Worked example

L3, two players. The buffet's columns are left: {K15} {K37} {K43}, middle: {K19} {K05} {K26}, right: {K49} {K13} {K06}. The cook stands at the middle. A's plate holds {K32} (a 6) and {K10} (a 2). B's plate holds {K20} (a 4).

  1. The dice show 4 and 3: the appetite is 7 (added) or 1 (4 minus 3). A can reach the middle and right columns. A takes Idhayan (1) (a 1) and Bharati (5) (a 5) from the middle. Sharada (6) plus Idhayan (1) is 6 plus 1 = 7. A serves and takes a star. A keeps Ammlu (2) and Bharati (5). The cook stays at the middle. The pile fills the gaps with Amay (1) (a 1) and Bn Sharada (2) (a 2).

  2. New dice, 5 and 3: the appetite is 8 or 2. B can reach the middle (Amyra (4), Amay (1), Bn Sharada (2)) and the right. B takes Amyra (4) (a 4) and Bn Sharada (2) (a 2). Gopi (4) plus Amyra (4) is 4 plus 4 = 8. B serves and takes a star. B keeps Bn Sharada (2) on the plate.

  3. Rainbow Camp mode: a pack of Amyra (4), Avika (4) and Amyra (5) shows Red and Green, Orange and Yellow, Blue and Purple: all six colours, a Rainbow set, 10 points. Sharada (6), Gopi (5) and Pinku (2) all wear suit 1: a suit trio, 6 points. A bond pair such as Idhayan (1) (1) and Smaya (8) (8) adds to 9: 3 points.

  4. Expedition Photo mode: Shreya (2) and Shreya (7) are twins (both Shreya) and both Tigers, side by side. Put Kanasu (3), another Tiger, next to them in the same row. Two Tiger neighbours score 1 each, the twins score 3 more, and a full row of one team scores 4 more: 9 points.

Level ladder

L1 · age 5

Age 5. One die is the appetite (1 to 6). Serve with 1, 2 or 3 cards. First to 4 stars.

L2 · ages 6 to 7

Ages 6 to 7. Two dice added (2 to 12). Serve with 2 or 3 cards. Say the number of each card you take out loud.

L3 · age 8 and up

Age 8 and up. Two dice: serve either the sum or the difference. Or play a Mode: Rainbow Camp or Expedition Photo (see below).

Solo

Cook alone against the draw pile. Play until you have served 4 guests and count your turns. Fewer is better. L1: Gold 5, Silver 6, Bronze 7. L2: Gold 6, Silver 7, Bronze 8. L3: Gold 5, Silver 6, Bronze 8. Modes solo: Rainbow Camp, 5 turns: Bronze 20, Silver 21, Gold 22. Expedition Photo, 5 turns: Bronze 13, Silver 16, Gold 19.

Two players

Works as written. With two players the next player always has the choice you leave them, so think one move ahead. A tie at 4 stars is settled by fewer cards on the plate.

Maths and skills in this game

Adding to a target with 2 or 3 numbers, the difference of two dice (L3), planning ahead with the cook. Rainbow: sets of three colours, counting to 22. Photo: neighbours, rows and columns.

Variants and options

  • RAINBOW CAMP (Mode): same take-two turn, no appetite. Roll the Suit key die at the start of each turn: any card you take that wears that suit scores +1 now. Keep a pack of 6 cards (throw extras face up). After 5 turns each, score sets from your pack, each card in one set only: Rainbow (3 cards that together show all six colours) 10, suit trio (3 cards sharing a suit) 6, bond pair (two cards adding to 9, or two 9s) 3. Most points wins; tie: more suit bonus, then share.

  • EXPEDITION PHOTO (Mode): same take-two turn. Each player builds a 3 by 3 photo of face-up cards, placed permanently as taken (the fifth turn takes just one card). Roll the Team key die at the start of each turn: each card you take of that team scores +1 now. At the end score every side-by-side pair of the same team 1, twins side by side +3 more, and a whole row or column of one team +4. Most points wins; tie: more team bonus, then share.

Which card elements do the work

NumberRule Kitchen: your plate must add to the appetite. Rainbow: bond pairs
ColoursRule Rainbow Camp: all six colours in a set
Suit pairRule Rainbow Camp: suit trios and the suit die bonus
Back patternNot used
TeamRule Expedition Photo: team runs and the team die bonus
Letter tileNot used
SerialNot used
NamesRule Expedition Photo: twins side by side score; Kitchen: say the name of the cards you take
ExpressionNot used
PlaceNot used

  • Model: take any 2 from the cook's column or the one to its right (wrapping), and the cook moves to the column taken. This is a Point Salad style market with a cook pawn. With 3 columns, an 'adjacent' rule would let you reach all of them, so the rule is 'cook's column or the next one': 2 of 3 columns every turn.

  • Kitchen games to 4 stars are short: total turns of all players with smart bots are 2 players 10 (L1), 12 (L2), 12 (L3); 3 players 14, 18, 18; 4 players 18, 23, 23. At about 10 seconds a turn that is 2 to 4 minutes, plus dice. Suggested: 4 stars as the minimum (a judgement, not simulated); 5 and 6 stars were worse, with 4 players tied 49% and 55% of games.

  • A look-ahead bot (serves when it can, keeps a flexible plate, avoids leaving the next player a serve) beats random players 89 / 83 / 72% (2 / 3 / 4 players, L1; fair 50 / 33 / 25), 92 / 87 / 76% at L2 and 94 / 88 / 77% at L3. Equal-skill bots win 48 / 38 / 25% from the first seat at L1 and 47 / 34 / 28% at L2, so the first seat has no clear edge.

  • Four-player L2 games tied 15% and L3 18% at 4 stars, before the 'fewer cards on the plate' tie-break was added (the tie-break was not measured again). The guest leaves after a quiet round 1 to 2 times a game (0.6 to 2.1 per game), with no stalls and no endless games.

  • Solo Kitchen, turns to serve 4 guests with the look-ahead bot, 25th / 50th / 75th percent: L1 5 / 6 / 7, L2 6 / 7 / 8, L3 5 / 6 / 8. Random play needs 8 to 9 turns. The medals use these.

  • Rainbow Camp (Mode): a pack of 6 (keep your best 6, throw the rest face up) makes the bot beat random 98 / 96 / 94% (2 / 3 / 4 players), scoring 21 / 22 / 23 against random 11 / 14 / 16, over 5 turns each (10 / 15 / 20 turns in total). Sets are a Rainbow (3 cards, all six colours) 10, a suit trio 6, a bond pair 3. Testing changed the rule to the pack of 6: with all collected cards (13 to 15 per player) every smart player scored about 22 (quartiles 22 / 22 / 22), the game tied in 19 to 33% of runs and the best bot beat random only 80%. Ties are still 17 / 25 / 33% because scores cluster around 22, so ties are a risk; suggested tie-break, not simulated: suit-die bonus first, then share the win.

  • Expedition Photo (Mode): the bot beats random 99 / 97 / 98%, with median score 17 (quartiles 14 and 20) against 4 (2 to 6) for random players, so almost all of the skill is in the placing. Neighbours of the same team score 1 each, twins side by side +3, a full row or column of one team +4, and the team die gives +1 for each card of that team you take. Ties are 3 / 8 / 10% of games, and 2 to 3% once the bonus is the tie-break. Length is 5 turns each (the fifth turn takes one card): 10 / 15 / 20 turns in total.

  • Solo Rainbow (5 turns): smart bot 20 / 21 / 22 (25th / 50th / 75th); random 11 / 14 / 16. Solo Photo: smart 13 / 16 / 19; random 2 / 4 / 6.

Not tested:

  • Not tested: a greedy bot against the look-ahead bot, in any mode, so the share of obvious picks is not measured. A related market-draft model gave obvious picks of 50 down to 28% and a look-ahead edge of 61%.

  • Not tested: denial in Rainbow and Photo. Their bots do not stop the next player; the Kitchen bot does.

  • Not tested: the Mode rules at levels beyond L1-style settings. The suit and team dice bonuses were used but their effect was not measured separately.

  • Not tested: Kitchen with 5 stars, or a plate of 4 or 6, beyond the 5 and 6 stars test.

Front

CAMP KITCHEN. Hungry guests arrive. The cook can only reach part of the buffet. NEED: all the cards, 1 or 2 dice, 1 pawn (the cook). SET UP: lay a 3 by 3 buffet, put the cook at the middle column. HOW TO PLAY: on your turn take any 2 cards from the cook's column or the one to its right (the edge wraps). The cook moves to the column you took from. Fill the gaps. If cards on your plate add up exactly to the guest's appetite, serve: put them down, take a star, roll a new guest. Plate: 5 cards at most. First to 4 stars wins. Quiet round: new guest.

Same team side by side 1, twins +3, a row or column of one team +4. Team die: +1 per card of that team. SOLO medals (turns to 4 stars): L1 5 / 6 / 7, L2 6 / 7 / 8, L3 5 / 6 / 8.

Kids only · Game 6 of 12 · Closest number wins · Fronts

Bullseye Ridge

Roll the target stone. The climber who lands nearest the mark wins the ledge.

KidsFamilyEasy
Game code
KO-06
Players
1 to 5
Time
10 to 15 min
Age
5+
Dice
1 die (L1) · 2 dice (L2, L3)
Pawns
None

Times include about 20% for learning the rules and for thinking. The raw simulated lengths are in the stats for nerds.

The whole game in one line

Roll a target. Everyone plays one card face down. The number nearest the target wins the round and scores the target. Spread your hand: you only get each card once.

What you need

All 54 cards6 cards each (8 at L3), dealt twice
1 die at L1, 2 dice at L2 and L3the target; dice are just numbers here
Pencil and paperto count points

Fronts of the cards are private, backs are public. Reference cards are the seven small cards in the box (Ref 1 to 7).

Set up

  • Shuffle. Deal 6 cards to each player (8 at L3). Keep them secret. Put the rest aside.

  • Play 6 rounds with these cards (4 rounds at L3). That is one ridge. Then shuffle all 54 and deal again for a second ridge.

  • Two players: add a Ghost. Each round it plays the top card of the deck (two cards at L3).

  • Use paper to keep score. Youngest rolls first.

How to play

Each round:

  1. Roll the target. L1: one die. L2 and L3: both dice, added (2 to 12). Say it out loud.

  2. Everyone chooses a card and puts it face down. L3: choose two cards and add their numbers.

  3. Turn them over together. The distance is the difference between the number and the target (a 7 and a target of 4 is distance 3).

  4. The smallest distance wins. The winner scores the target number and 3 more for a bullseye (distance 0).

  5. Tie on distance: a card that adds to 9 with the target wins. Still tied: the higher serial wins (the small number in the pill under the letter tile). No two serials are the same.

How it ends

After the second ridge, most points wins. Tie: lower total distance over the game; still tied, share the win.

Words in this game

  • Target The number rolled. Win by landing nearest it.
  • Distance How far your number is from the target. Subtract the smaller from the bigger.
  • Bullseye Distance 0. Scores 3 extra.
  • Ridge One deal of cards, 6 rounds (4 at L3).
  • Serial The small number from 1 to 54 in the pill under the letter tile. Not the big number.

Common questions

  • Why do I not just play my closest card every time? You can, and it wins the round, but the cards go away. High targets pay more points, so keep your good cards for them.

  • What if the target is 12 and my best card is a 9? At L2 and L3 the target goes up to 12. A 9 is distance 3. Plan for it: keep your 9 for a big target.

  • How can two cards tie and still have a winner? The tie-break says a card that adds with the target to 9 wins, then the higher serial. Serials are all different, so a round always has one winner.

  • What does the Ghost do? It plays the top card of the deck every round. It can win rounds and score, so you have to beat it too.

  • Do I keep played cards? No. They are used up.

Tips

  • Do not always play the closest card. High targets score the target number (plus 3 for a bullseye), so saving a 9 for a big target is worth more than winning a small round. Planning added about 7 to 10 points in testing.

  • Count what has been played. The planning bot also counts cards used, so at L2 and L3 you can guess which targets your high cards can still reach.

  • Know the tie-breaks: a card that adds to 9 with the target wins a distance tie, then the higher serial. Ties on distance happen in 28% to 66% of rounds, so a bond card can be the winning card.

  • At L3 you play two cards and add them, so pick the pair that lands nearest the target and keep a pair for the other big rounds.

  • With a 5-year-old, say the distance out loud each round ('7 and 4, that is 3 away'). Subtraction becomes a real game, and the Ghost in the 2-player game keeps ties from deciding every round.

Worked example

Three players, L2 for the first three rounds. Every card used is thrown away afterwards.

  1. Target: the dice show 5 and 2, so 7. A plays Bharati (4) (4), distance 3. B plays Rihansh (9) (9), distance 2. C plays Pinku (2) (2), distance 5. B wins and scores 7.

  2. Target: the dice show 3 and 2, so 5. A plays Dharsh (2) (2), distance 3. B plays Nakul (4) (4), distance 1. C plays Naresh (6) (6), distance 1. B and C tie. B's 4 adds to 9 with the target 5, so B wins and scores 5.

  3. Target: the dice show 4 and 2, so 6. A plays Bharati (5) (5), distance 1. B plays Shreya (7) (7), distance 1. C plays Smaya (8) (8), distance 2. A and B tie, and neither card adds to 9 with 6. Serial decides: Bharati (5) is 51 and Shreya (7) is 6, so A wins and scores 6.

  4. L3, a different game. The dice show 6 and 4, so the target is 10. A plays Bharati (4) and Avika (5): 4 plus 5 is 9, distance 1. B plays Adheesh (9) and Smaya (1): 9 plus 1 is 10, distance 0, a bullseye. C plays Amyra (4) and Smaya (8): 4 plus 8 is 12, distance 2. B wins and scores 10 plus 3, which is 13.

Level ladder

L1 · age 5

Age 5. One die is the target (1 to 6). Play one card from 6. Winner scores the target, plus 3 for a bullseye. 12 rounds in two ridges.

L2 · ages 6 to 7

Ages 6 to 7. Two dice added: the target is 2 to 12. Big targets are worth a lot, so save your high cards. Say each distance out loud.

L3 · age 8 and up

Age 8 and up. Hold 8 cards and play two each round: their sum should land nearest the target. 4 rounds per ridge, two ridges.

Solo

Climb against the Ghost. You and the Ghost play every round; the Ghost plays the top card(s) of the deck. Play the two ridges and subtract the Ghost's points from yours. L1: Bronze 5, Silver 17, Gold 28. L2: Bronze 4, Silver 26, Gold 44. L3: Bronze 8, Silver 26, Gold 42. A bot that plays the closest card beat the Ghost 82%, 79%, 84% of games at L1, L2, L3.

Two players

Add the Ghost as a third player: it plays the top card of the deck (two cards at L3) each round. This lowers the chance of a tie between just the two of you and gives a fair 3-way race.

Maths and skills in this game

Subtraction as distance (bigger minus smaller), adding two dice to 12, adding two cards at L3, bonds to 9 as a tie-break, planning a hand across rounds.

Which card elements do the work

NumberRule the card number is your guess; distance is a subtraction
ColoursNot used
Suit pairNot used
Back patternNot used
TeamNot used
Letter tileNot used
SerialRule final tie-break, always unique
NamesFlavour say the name of the explorer you play
ExpressionNot used
PlaceNot used

Not tested:

  • Not tested: bluffing or reading other players. Bots hear nothing about what other players hold; children may bluff or read each other.

  • Not tested as written: five players at L3 (10 cards a round from a deck of 54) was simulated, but a second ridge shuffles used cards, a small difference from the written rule.

Two players add a Ghost that plays the top card of the deck. HOW TO PLAY: each round roll the target (L1 one die, L2 two dice added). Everyone plays one card face down (L3 two cards added). Kids only · Game 7 of 12 · Snatch and empty · Fronts

Camp Raid

The camp is asleep and the stashes are open. A quick hand, a good number, and a card changes sides.

Inspired by Kolkata Thieves and Clumsy Thief

KidsEasy
Game code
KO-07
Players
1 to 5
Time
10 to 15 min
Age
5+
Dice
None at L1 · Team die at L2 and up (Team key, Ref 4)
Pawns
None

Times include about 20% for learning the rules and for thinking. The raw simulated lengths are in the stats for nerds.

The whole game in one line

Each player has a hand and a face-up stash. Snatch the top card of someone's stash with a card that adds to 9 with it. The first to empty their hand wins.

What you need

All 54 cardshand of 5, 6 or 7, a 2-card stash each, the rest a stock
1 dieL2 and up · Team key, Ref 4

Fronts of the cards are private, backs are public. Reference cards are the seven small cards in the box (Ref 1 to 7).

Set up

  • Shuffle. Deal each player a hand: 5 cards (L1), 6 (L2) or 7 (L3). Keep it secret.

  • Deal each player 2 more cards face up in one pile: your stash. Only the top card counts. Everyone sees it.

  • Put the rest face down as the stock.

  • Two players: turn one card face up from the stock as a Ghost stash. It never plays but you can snatch from it. Youngest starts.

How to play

On your turn:

  1. L2 and up: roll the die and read it on the Team key (Ref 4). That team is guarded this turn: you cannot snatch a top card from that team.

  2. Snatch if you can. Choose another stash whose top card is not guarded, and a card in your hand that adds to 9 with that top card (1 and 8, 2 and 7, 3 and 6, 4 and 5, or two 9s). Put your card on your own stash. Send their top card to the bottom of the stock. If you can snatch, you must.

  3. If their stash is empty after a snatch, they turn the top card of the stock onto it.

  4. No snatch? Swap: put one card from your hand on the bottom of the stock and take the top card of the stock. Your turn ends.

  5. L3: a 9 is a wildcard. It can snatch any top card, and any card can snatch a top 9. Also, once per game, if you have no other snatch you may sneak: snatch a guarded top card that bonds.

How it ends

When you play your last card you shout “Camp clear!” and sit out. Finish the round so everyone has had the same number of turns. Empty hand wins. If two or more players are clear, the one with the most cards in their stash wins (tie: the higher serial on top of the stash).

Words in this game

  • Stash Your face-up pile. Only the top card can be snatched.
  • Snatch Play a card that adds to 9 with an opponent's top card. Their card goes to the stock and yours lands on your stash.
  • Guarded team The team on the die this turn. A top card of that team is safe.
  • Bond Two numbers that add to 9. A 9 only bonds with a 9 (at L3 a 9 is wild).
  • Sneak L3, once per game: snatch a guarded top card when you have no other snatch.

Common questions

  • Do I have to snatch? Yes, if you can. Snatching is how you empty your hand. If two snatches are possible, choose the one you like.

  • Why can I not swap when I can snatch? The swap is only for turns with no snatch. It keeps the game moving.

  • What if I hold a 9 at L1 or L2? A 9 only snatches a top 9. It is hard to use, so swap it away if it stays in your hand.

  • What does my stash do for me? Nothing for your hand, but it is a target. A card you place on your stash can be snatched by others, so think what it bonds with.

  • Is this a speed game? No. It is played in turns, so a five-year-old and an eight-year-old can play together.

Tips

  • Look at what bonds to your top card before you place a card on your stash. Whatever you put there can be snatched by anyone holding its partner to 9, so avoid a number whose partners are common in hands.

  • Hold your nines carefully. A 9 only bonds with another 9 at L1 and L2, so swap it away if it sits in your hand; at L3 a 9 is wild and becomes your best snatching card.

  • Choose the stash to hit. If two snatches are possible, pick the one that empties a rival or leaves you the best new top card. The bot that chose well and kept its nines won 4 to 6 points over random play.

  • Say the guarded team before you look at your hand at L2. A team on the die cannot be snatched this turn, so check your own stash for a card of that team and keep it there.

  • With a 5-year-old, play L1 with a hand of 5 and say 'what makes 9 with that?' before each turn. A lone 5-card hand has a bond to a given top card 46% of the time, so most turns the child has a real snatch.

Worked example

L3, three players. The tops of the stashes at the start are {K47} (A), {K39} (B) and {K06} (C).

  1. A rolls a 2 on the Team key: Elephants are guarded. A holds Smaya (8) (an 8), which would bond with C's Anayka (1) (a 1) but Anayka (1) is an Elephant, so it is guarded. A holds Dharsh (2) (a 2): 2 plus 7 is 9, and B's top Ajay (7) is a Cobra, not guarded. A plays Dharsh (2) on A's own stash and sends Ajay (7) to the bottom of the stock.

  2. B rolls a 5: Peacocks are guarded. A's top is now Dharsh (2), an Elephant, so it is open. B holds Shreya (7), a 7: 7 plus 2 is 9. B snatches. Dharsh (2) goes to the stock, Shreya (7) lands on B's stash. A's top is Arvind (8) again.

  3. C rolls a 1: Tigers are guarded. A's top Arvind (8) is a Monkey, so it is open. C holds Gowri (9), a 9. At L3 a 9 is wild, so C snatches Arvind (8). Gowri (9) lands on C's stash.

  4. Each snatch used one card from the snatcher's hand, so A has 6 cards left, B and C 6 each (they started with 7).

Level ladder

L1 · age 5

Age 5. Hand of 5. No dice, no guard. Snatch with a bond, or swap. Empty hand wins.

L2 · ages 6 to 7

Ages 6 to 7. Hand of 6. Roll the Team die each turn: that team is guarded. Say the name of the explorer you take.

L3 · age 8 and up

Age 8 and up. Hand of 7. A 9 is a wildcard, and you may sneak once per game to snatch a guarded card.

Solo

Raid the sleeping camp. Set up as for 3 players but the other two stashes are Ghosts that never play. Count your turns until you clear your hand (the Ghost stashes refill from the stock). Fewer turns is better. L1: Gold 13 or fewer, Silver 17, Bronze 23. L2: Gold 16, Silver 21, Bronze 28. L3: Gold 11, Silver 14, Bronze 17.

Two players

Add a Ghost stash (one card, face up, never plays). Without it, two players would run out of tops to snatch and the game stalled in about 1 game in 20 in testing. With a Ghost there were no stalls.

Maths and skills in this game

Bonds to 9 under time pressure. Seeing which numbers an opponent's stash can be broken by. L3: thinking about which card to place on top so it cannot be snatched.

Variants and options

  • Also known as 'Nine Heist' (the same snatch-by-bond idea).

Which card elements do the work

NumberRule snatching is a bond to 9
ColoursNot used
Suit pairNot used
Back patternNot used
TeamRule the team die guards one team each turn (L2 and up)
Letter tileNot used
SerialRule final tie-break between two clear players
NamesFlavour L2: say the explorer's name
ExpressionNot used
PlaceNot used

Lengths in this section are raw simulated times, without the learning and thinking allowance.

Status: Simulated. no stalls after four fixes (up to 58% before); smart edge 4 to 6 points; 4 to 7 min at 10 s a turn

SettingResult
2p L1 (Ghost)median 26 turns; smart bot 49% (50 even); snatch available 31% of turns
3p L133 turns; smart 32% (33 even); snatch 34%
4p L128 turns; smart 27% (25 even); snatch 51%

5p L335 turns; first seat wins 12% (20 even): risk
Solo (turns to clear)L1 13 / 17 / 23; L2 16 / 21 / 28; L3 11 / 14 / 17

  • Final rules, 1,200 games per setting: no stalls anywhere (about 40,000 games). Median total turns (all players): L1 26 / 33 / 28 / 30 for 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 players, L2 32 / 42 / 36 / 35, L3 20 / 27 / 32 / 35. At about 10 seconds a turn that is 4 to 7 minutes of play.

  • The first version stalled badly: in 200 games per setting, 11% to 21% of L1 games, 16% to 20% of L2 games and 26% to 58% of L3 games never finished in 400 turns (L1 with 3 players 42, L3 with 2 players 116). Sending a snatched card back to the stock, not to the snatcher's stash, took L1 with 3 to 5 players from 30 to 42 stalled games out of 200 to 0 (two players got worse, 46 of 200), and refilling an empty stash from the stock cut two-player L1 stalls from 46 to 22 of 200.

  • Letting two 9s bond and making the L3 wild nine work both ways (a 9 in hand snatches anything, anything snatches a top 9) cut L3 stalls from 124 / 92 / 43 of 200 (2 / 3 / 4 players) to 0 / 1 / 4, and L1 with two players from 22 to 9. With two players there is only one top to snatch, so a Ghost stash was added, taking 2-player L1 stalls from 9 of 200 to 0.

  • Finishing the round, instead of ending the moment someone cleared, evened out the seats: the first seat won 37.5% with three equal bots (33 fair) and 29% with four (25 fair) before, and 33.5% and 25% after. With equal bots no seat is favoured at L1 and L2 (first seat 52 / 33 / 23 / 18 at L1), but at L3 with 5 players the first seat wins only 12% (fair 20), because later seats get the last say when a round finishes. Suggested for 5 players at L3: a hand of 6 (not simulated).

  • A player had a legal snatch on 31% (2 players), 34% (3), 51% (4), 64% (5) of L1 turns, and on 54%, 56%, 70%, 80% at L3 with wild nines and bigger hands. A lone 5-card hand has a bond to a given top card 46% of the time; the rest of the miss is the guard, shrinking hands and few tops. A game has about 8 to 20 snatches at L1 and 13 to 31 at L3.

  • Skill is small at L1 and L2: a bot that picks which stash to hit and keeps its nines wins 49 / 32 / 27 / 22% at L1 (fair 50 / 33 / 25 / 20) against random players, and 53 / 36 / 25 / 22 at L2. At L3 it is 52 / 39 / 34 / 27. It is mostly luck at L1 and L2, which suits age 5, and a few points of skill at L3.

  • L3 additions: the wild nine shortens the game a lot (3 players 45 turns to 29) and adds 3 to 5 points of skill at 3 and 4 players. The sneak does nothing measurable (length 29 against 31 without it, edge 39% against 37%), so it stays as a one-time surprise, not as strategy.

  • Solo, 1,500 games a level, two Ghost stashes: turns to clear at the 25th / 50th / 75th percent: L1 13 / 17 / 23, L2 16 / 21 / 28, L3 11 / 14 / 17.

Not tested:

  • Not tested: the 'real-time snatching' of Kolkata Thieves. It is written as turns, so a bot can play it. A real-time version would give the fastest reader the win and is not recommended for a mixed 5-to-8 table.

  • Not tested: the suggested hand of 6 for 5 players at L3.

  • Not tested: the tie-break between two clear players (higher serial on the stash top); the simulation picked at random. Two or more players are clear in the same round in 5% (2 players) to 31% (5 players) of L1 games, and in 49% of 5-player L3 games.

  • Not tested: children hiding their stash tops or forgetting the guard.

Rule card text

Text for the printed card (63.5 x 88.9 mm). Layout comes later.

Front

CAMP RAID. The camp is asleep and the stashes are open. A quick hand and a good number: a card changes sides. NEED: all the cards. At L2 and up, a die (Team key, Ref 4). SET UP: deal a hand (5, 6 or 7) and a 2-card face-up stash to each player. The rest is the stock. Two players: add a Ghost stash. HOW TO PLAY: roll the Team die (L2 up): that team is guarded. Snatch an opponent's top stash card with a card from your hand that adds to 9 with it. Your card goes on your stash, theirs back to the stock. No snatch: swap one hand card with the stock. If you can snatch, you must. Empty your hand to win; finish the round, most stash cards breaks a tie.

Back

CAMP RAID: LEVELS. L1 (age 5): hand of 5, no die. L2 (ages 6 to 7): hand of 6, the Team die guards one team each turn. L3 (age 8 and up): hand of 7. A 9 is a wildcard. Once per game you may sneak and snatch a guarded card. BONDS: 1+8 2+7 3+6 4+5, 9 with 9. SOLO: two Ghost stashes. Count turns to clear. L1: Gold 13, Silver 17, Bronze 23. L2: Gold 16, Silver 21, Bronze 28. L3: Gold 11, Silver 14, Bronze 17. TWO PLAYERS: add a Ghost stash.

Kids only · Game 8 of 12 · Race along the backs · Backs (Colour trail uses fronts)

Trail Run

The trail winds up the hill. Follow the signs on the backs of the cards and run to the top and back.

Inspired by includes the Colour trail mode

KidsFamilyEasy
Game code
KO-08
Players
2 to 5
Time
10 to 15 min
Age
5+
Dice
1 die (L1) · 2 dice (L2) · 3 dice (L3)
Pawns
1 runner each

Times include about 20% for learning the rules and for thinking. The raw simulated lengths are in the stats for nerds.

The whole game in one line

Lay cards back up in a snake. Roll the die, read the suit on the Suit key, and jump your runner to the next card whose back shows that suit. Run to the end of the trail and back first.

What you need

All 54 cards12 to 24 laid back up as the trail
1 die2 dice at L2, 3 at L3
REF 4the Suit key (other side)
1 pawn eachyour runner

Fronts of the cards are private, backs are public. Reference cards are the seven small cards in the box (Ref 1 to 7).

Set up

  • Shuffle all the cards. Lay 12 cards (L1), 20 (L2) or 24 (L3) back up in a long snake, a few cards to a row, so the trail winds like a path. The first card is the start, the last is the top.

  • Each player puts a pawn just before the first card. Put the Suit key (Ref 4) where everyone can see it.

  • Look at the picture on a back: it is a grid of 2 columns and 3 rows, so six slots, numbered 1 to 6 left to right, top to bottom. Each slot holds one suit.

  • Youngest goes first, then play passes to the left.

How to play

On your turn:

  1. L1: roll the die and read the suit on the Suit key. Move your pawn forward to the next card whose back shows that suit anywhere. You may jump over many cards.

  2. L2: roll two dice. The first is the suit. The second is the slot (1 to 6). Move forward to the next card that shows that suit in that slot.

  3. L3: roll three dice. Two are suits and the third is the slot. Choose one of the two suits and use it with the slot, as at L2.

  4. No card ahead matches? You have run off the end: you have reached the top.

  5. Out and back: at the top, turn round and run back down the same cards. On the way back the cards are read from the other end, so slot 1 is the last slot and slot 6 the first (count 7 minus the slot).

  6. Reach the start again, past the first card, and you are home.

How it ends

The first runner home wins. Finish the round so everyone has had the same number of turns. If more than one is home, they roll a die each and the highest roll wins (roll again on a tie). L2 and L3 with 2 or 3 players: play three trails, first to win two. With 4 or 5 players play one trail.

Words in this game

  • Trail the snake of cards laid back up. Your runner moves along it.
  • Slot one of six places on a back, numbered 1 to 6 (left to right, top to bottom).
  • Suit key Ref 4. The die number tells you which suit to look for.
  • Top the end of the trail. Run to it and back.
  • Colour trail the front-side version of the game, see Ladder.

Common questions

  • Can two runners stand on the same card? Yes. They do not block each other.

  • What if the suit is on the card I am standing on? That does not count. Always move forward to the next card.

  • Why do I read the slots the other way on the way back? You are walking the trail in the other direction, as if the cards were turned round. Slot 1 becomes the last slot.

  • What if I roll a suit no card ahead shows? You run off the end. Out, you reach the top. Back, you are home.

  • Are there choices? Not until L3, where you pick one of two suits. Pick the one that takes you further.

Tips

  • At L1 and L2 there are no choices, so keep the game moving and let the dice decide. The only real decision comes at L3, where you choose between two suits.

  • At L3 always check both suits and take the further jump. In testing that simple choice beat random picks 91% at 2 players in best of three.

  • On the way back read the slots the other way round: slot 1 is the last slot, so count 7 minus the slot. Say it aloud before every move on the return.

  • Finish the round so everyone has had the same number of turns, and roll off for a tie. Without this the first player won 58% of 2-player games, so remember to play it out.

  • With a 5-year-old, use L1 and let the child read the Suit key. A trail of 12 cards takes a median 13 rolls out and back alone, so a game is only about 4 to 8 minutes.

Worked example

L2. Six cards of the trail, in order from the start. Real cards. Backs are read as 2 columns by 3 rows, slots 1 to 6.

  1. The trail begins Adhiraa (3), Amay (8), Archana (5), Nakul (4), Sharada (3), Smaya (8). A and B stand before Adhiraa (3).

  2. A rolls suit 4 and slot 3. Neither Adhiraa (3) nor Amay (8) shows suit 4 in slot 3. Archana (5) does. A moves there.

  3. B rolls suit 1 and slot 5. Adhiraa (3) has a different suit in slot 5, but Amay (8) has suit 1 there. B moves to Amay (8).

  4. A rolls suit 5 and slot 6. Nakul (4) and Sharada (3) do not show suit 5 in slot 6, but Smaya (8) does. A jumps over two cards to Smaya (8).

  5. Later, running back, A is before Smaya (8) and rolls suit 5 and slot 6. Coming back, slot 6 is read as slot 1, and Smaya (8) shows suit 5 in slot 1. A moves on to it.

  6. At L1 the same first roll would be one die: suit 3. Adhiraa (3), Amay (8), Archana (5) and Nakul (4) do not show suit 3 anywhere, Sharada (3) does, and a runner at the start jumps four cards at once.

Level ladder

L1 · age 5

Age 5. One die: the suit anywhere on the back. A trail of 12 cards, out and back. A helper may read the Suit key.

L2 · ages 6 to 7

Ages 6 to 7. Two dice: suit plus slot, and a trail of 20. Counting slots and reading them backwards on the way back. Three trails for 2 or 3 players.

L3 · age 8 and up

Age 8 and up. Three dice: two suits (choose one) plus the slot, a trail of 24. Colour trail (front-side mode, any level): lay 20 cards front up, roll the die on the Colour key (Ref 3) and jump to the next card with that colour on its border. If the card you land on and the card you left have numbers that add to 9, roll again.

Solo

Beat the clock. Run out and back alone and count your rolls. Fewer is better. L1 (12 cards): Gold 11, Silver 13, Bronze 15. L2 (20 cards): Gold 7, Silver 8, Bronze 10. L3 (24 cards): Gold 6, Silver 7, Bronze 8. Colour trail (20 cards, one lap): Gold 6, Silver 8, Bronze 9.

Two players

As written. At L2 and L3 play three trails and the first to win two is the champion. Both runners roll their own dice.

Maths and skills in this game

Matching patterns, counting slots 1 to 6 and reading them backwards (7 minus the slot) on the way back. In the Colour trail, number bonds to 9.

Variants and options

  • Colour trail (a mode on the fronts: a trail of 20 cards, colour die, jump to the next card with that colour, bond re-roll). A back game cannot read fronts, so it is a separate mode.

Which card elements do the work

NumberRule only in the Colour trail: a bond to 9 with the card you left gives a re-roll
ColoursRule only in the Colour trail: the colour die picks the border colour to jump to
Suit pairNot used the suit on a back is used, not the pair on the front
Back patternRule the suits and slots on the back decide every move
TeamNot used
Letter tileNot used
SerialNot used
NamesFlavour say the name of the card you land on
ExpressionNot used
PlaceNot used

Stats for nerds: what the simulations showed

Lengths in this section are raw simulated times, without the learning and thinking allowance.

Status: Simulated. Out and back, round finished, roll-off for ties: seats within 2 points of fair; L1 median 13 rolls alone; 4 to 9 min

SettingResult
L1 12 cards, 2 to 5 players4.0 / 5.5 / 7.3 / 8.3 min; ties 13% / 17% / 21% / 23%
L1 solomedian 13 rolls (11 to 15)
L2 20 cards, best of 3 (2 and 3p)5.7 / 9.0 min
L2 one trail (4 and 5p)4.0 / 5.0 min
L3 24 cards, smart vs random91% / 85% / 81% / 75% at 2 to 5p (best of 3)
Colour trail 20 cardssolo median 8 rolls; 2 to 5p 2.3 to 4.7 min

  • Bots on the real backs: a runner rolls and moves; there are no choices before L3, so the game is a pure dice race. 3,000 to 6,000 runs per setting.

  • The round is always finished, with a roll-off between the players who finish in the same round. A first try (one-way trail of 14 cards at L1, play stopping the moment someone arrived) gave the first player 58% of two-player games (50% is even) and 30% of five-player games (20% is even), and the fifth player 13%; with the change it is 51/49 at 2 players and 21/21/19/19/20 at 5 players. Ties before the roll-off were 13%, 17%, 21% and 23% for 2 to 5 players, which is why the roll-off is in the rules.

  • The trail is out and back because a one-way run was too short: 12 cards took a median 7 rolls each (middle half 6 to 8), so a 3-player game was about 3.5 minutes. Out and back takes 13 rolls alone at L1 (middle half 11 to 15, 90% within 8 to 17), and a game of 4.0 / 5.5 / 7.3 / 8.3 minutes for 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 players at 10 seconds a roll.

  • The slot die at L2 and L3 makes jumps much longer, because one card in six has the right suit in the right slot (against one in two for the suit anywhere): a 12-card run took 3 rolls instead of 7, spread 1 to 5. A slot die with a trail of 24 and a one-way run was a 5 roll median (3 to 8, 90%). That is why L2 uses 20 cards out and back (median 8 rolls alone, middle half 7 to 10) and L3 uses 24 (median 7, middle half 6 to 8), played as best of three trails for 2 or 3 players (5.7 and 9 minutes at L2, 5 and 8 minutes at L3). With 4 or 5 players one trail takes 4 and 5 minutes at L2 and 3.3 and 4.2 at L3, because best of three ran 13 to 16 minutes there.

  • L3 choice: choosing the further of two suits is an obvious move, but it is a real edge. In best of three, a bot that always takes the further jump beats random pickers 91% at 2 players, 85% at 3, 81% at 4 and 75% at 5 (fair share 50%, 33%, 25%, 20%). In a single trail the edge is 81%, 69%, 61% and 53%.

  • A bump rule (landing on another pawn sent it back one card) was tried and dropped. It changed nothing (smart win rate 0.910 against 0.908; length unchanged), so it was removed to keep the rules short.

  • Colour trail, 20 cards front up: median 8 rolls alone (middle half 6 to 9). The bond re-roll fires on 10% of jumps, once or twice a game, and does not change the number of rolls to the end, only who gets the extra turns. 2 to 5 players: 4.0 / 4.7 minutes at 4 and 5 players, ties 16% to 31%, seats even (50/50 at 2p, 25% each at 4p).

  • Backs: every suit sits in each slot on 9 of the 54 cards, so no slot or suit is easier. No stall is possible, since a run that finds no card simply ends.

Not tested:

  • Not tested: the cost to real children of reading slots 1 to 6 backwards on the way back.

  • Not tested: the out-and-back reading rule at L2 and L3 with children aged 6 to 7. It is the least certain part of the design.

  • Not tested: table space for 20 and 24 cards.

  • Not tested: player choice with the bond re-roll in the Colour trail. It was simulated only for turn order.

Rule card text

Text for the printed card (63.5 x 88.9 mm). Layout comes later.

Front

TRAIL RUN. Lay cards back up in a snake. Your pawn waits before the first card. Roll the die and read the suit on the Suit key (Ref 4). Move forward to the next card whose back shows that suit. Reach the top, turn round and run back along the same cards. First home wins. L2: a second die gives the slot (1 to 6): the card must show the suit in that slot. Coming back, count the slots from the other end. Everyone gets the same number of turns; tied runners roll off.

Back

LEVELS. L1: 12 cards, suit anywhere. L2: 20 cards, suit and slot, best of 3 trails for 2 or 3 players. L3: 24 cards, two suit dice (take one) plus the slot. COLOUR TRAIL: 20 cards front up, die on the Colour key (Ref 3), jump to the next card with that colour; a bond to 9 with the card you left means roll again. SOLO, rolls to run out and back, fewer is better. L1 Gold 11, Silver 13, Bronze 15. L2 Gold 7, Silver 8, Bronze 10. L3 Gold 6, Silver 7, Bronze 8.

Kids only · Game 9 of 12 · Silent team climb · Fronts

Quiet Climb

The mountain is silent and the whole team must climb it together, one quiet step after another.

Inspired by The Mind by Wolfgang Warsch

RecommendedKidsFamilyEasy
Game code
KO-09
Players
2 to 5
Time
10 to 15 min
Age
5+
Dice
None
Pawns
Shared pawns (lives)

Times include about 20% for learning the rules and for thinking. The raw simulated lengths are in the stats for nerds.

The whole game in one line

Everyone holds a few cards. Without talking, the team lays them face up in order of the serial number, smallest first. Each mistake costs the team a pawn.

What you need

All 54 cardsdeal 1, 2 or 3 each, every climb
Pawnsplayers + 1, shared by the team (the team's lives)
Ref 4the Team key, for L3 (animal names)

Fronts of the cards are private, backs are public. Reference cards are the seven small cards in the box (Ref 1 to 7).

Set up

  • Put the pawns in the middle of the table. Use one more pawn than there are players (2 players: 3 pawns, 5 players: 6). These are the team's lives.

  • Shuffle all 54 cards. Deal 1 card each at L1, 2 at L2, 3 at L3. Look at your cards. Keep them secret.

  • Find the serial on each card: the small number from 1 to 54 in the pill under the letter tile. Not the big number.

  • Sit round the table. Hands flat. Breathe together three times, then begin. No talking, no pointing, no signals.

How to play

Each climb:

  1. Anyone may lay a card at any moment: put your smallest serial face up in the middle. There is no turn order. You decide when it is time, by feeling how far the number is from the last one.

  2. The cards must go down smallest serial first, from all hands mixed together. The first card has to be low to be safe, a big gap means wait longer.

  3. A mistake happens when someone lays a card and another player still holds a smaller serial. Everyone shows their smaller cards and they are put aside. The team loses 1 pawn, however many cards were wrong. Then keep going.

  4. The climb is over when every card is laid or put aside. Perfect climb (no mistake): the team wins a pawn back, up to the pawns it started with. Shuffle everything and deal the next climb.

  5. L3 only, the hold: if your smallest card is on the same team as the card just laid (same animal on the Team key, Ref 4), you must hold. Do not lay it. When the next card goes down, lay your held cards that are smaller than it straight away, smallest first. They are safe. If you lay a card straight after a card of its own team, that is a mistake.

How it ends

You win when you finish the last climb with at least 1 pawn. You lose when the last pawn is gone. Climbs: 7 at L1, 6 at L2, 5 at L3. Medals: Bronze finish. Silver finish with at least half your starting pawns. Gold finish with at most 1 pawn lost.

Words in this game

  • Serial the small number from 1 to 54 in the pill under the letter tile. This is the number you climb in, not the big number on the card.
  • Climb one deal of cards, played until every card is laid or put aside.
  • Pawn one of the team's lives. Lose one on every mistake.
  • Hold L3: your smallest card shares a team with the card just laid, so you wait one card.

Common questions

  • Can we talk, nod or count aloud? No. If you do, count it as a mistake and lose a pawn. You may count in your head as slowly as you like.

  • What if two people lay at the same time? Lay them both. If they are in the wrong order, it is a mistake. If the lower one went first, fine.

  • What if I held a card and the next player lays a card lower than mine? Lay yours. Anything laid is fine as long as nobody holds a smaller serial.

  • Why can I not see everyone's cards? Fronts are private. Backs are public, but the backs tell you nothing about the serial.

  • Why does a hold not cost a pawn? A hold is only waiting, and the held card is safe from the next card. The pawn is lost only if you lay a card of the same team straight after a card of its team.

Tips

  • Count the gap in your head and wait in proportion. A big gap between your smallest serial and the last card means wait longer, and the game is won by how little players differ in pace, not by speed.

  • Do not lay a first card too early. The first card has to be low to be safe, so with a middle serial in hand take a slow breath before you move.

  • At L3 check the team of the card just laid. If your smallest card is on the same team you must hold, and the hold is safe: lay it when the next card goes down. In testing a hold came up in most climbs.

  • The win-back pawn matters. A perfect climb wins a pawn back, and without it a decent team at L2 falls from 90% to 78% at 2 players, so play the early climbs carefully to stay ahead.

  • With a 5-year-old, play L1 with one card each and breathe the beat for the group. Let the child decide when to lay, and say 'we all counted differently' after a mistake rather than blaming.

Worked example

L3, two players, 3 pawns, three cards each. A holds {K31}, {K38} and {K34}. B holds {K49}, {K44} and {K52}. All real cards from the deck.

  1. The serials: Naresh (6) 16, Gowri (9) 18, Pinku (7) 26, Nysha (8) 41, Adhiraa (6) 47, Adheesh (9) 49. Nobody knows the other player's numbers. Naresh (6) is the smallest of all six, so A feels it is the lowest and lays it first. It is a Bear.

  2. B lays Gowri (9), serial 18, a Cobra. It is above 16, so it is safe.

  3. A's smallest card is Pinku (7), serial 26, and it is a Cobra too, the same team as the card just laid. A must hold. B waits and then lays Nysha (8), serial 41, a Monkey.

  4. Straight after, A lays Pinku (7). It is smaller than 41 but safe because it was held. Had A laid it right after Gowri (9), it would have been a mistake: both Cobras in a row, lose a pawn.

  5. A lays Adhiraa (6), serial 47, a Tiger. B lays Adheesh (9), serial 49, a Bear. All six cards are down with no mistake. It is a perfect climb, so the team wins back a pawn (up to the start of 3).

Level ladder

L1 · age 5

Age 5. One card each. Lay it when you think it is time. Seven climbs, players + 1 pawns. A helper may breathe the beat for the group.

L2 · ages 6 to 7

Ages 6 to 7. Two cards each. Your smaller card goes first, and then you decide when to lay the next. Six climbs.

L3 · age 8 and up

Age 8 and up. Three cards each, five climbs, plus the team hold rule.

Solo

Ghost Climb. Take N cards in your hand (3 at L1, 4 at L2, 5 at L3) and N more face down in a row as the Ghost. Each step, either lay your smallest card, or flip the next Ghost card. Cards rise from the start. A slip is a flipped Ghost card smaller than the last card, or bigger than a card you still hold (that card is put aside). Count slips. Lantern: once a game you may peek at the next Ghost card. Medals (fewer slips is better): L1 Gold 1 or fewer, Silver 2, Bronze 3. L2 Gold 1, Silver 2, Bronze 3. L3 Gold 2, Silver 3, Bronze 4.

Two players

As written, with 3 pawns. Each of you holds your own sequence, which makes it easiest to feel the other's timing. With a good tempo most pairs win.

Maths and skills in this game

Comparing numbers up to 54, estimating gaps, counting up silently as a pace. At L3 noticing which team a card is on.

Which card elements do the work

NumberNot used the big card number does not matter in this game
ColoursNot used
Suit pairNot used
Back patternNot used
TeamRule at L3 a card on the same team as the last card must be held
Letter tileNot used
SerialRule the whole game: lay cards in rising serial order
NamesFlavour say the child's name when you lay
ExpressionNot used
PlaceNot used

Stats for nerds: what the simulations showed

Lengths in this section are raw simulated times, without the learning and thinking allowance.

Status: Simulated. L2 win rate: decent teams 90% / 76% / 60% / 50% at 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 players; median 6.5 min; results range widely from novice to tuned teams

SettingResult
L1 2 to 5p, decent99% / 98% / 96% / 94%, about 7 min
L1 novice96% / 91% / 79% / 69%
L2 decent90% / 76% / 60% / 50%, about 6.5 min
L2 novice / tuned76% to 7% / 98% to 94%
L3 decent82% / 62% / 43% / 30%, about 5.5 min
Random timingL1 58% at 2p, 17% at 3p, 0 at L2 above 2p
Solo ghost mean slips2.0 / 2.9 / 3.9 (3, 4, 5 cards); lantern 1.5 / 2.3 / 3.3

  • This is a timing game, so it was simulated with a model of human timing, not with real people. Each player waits a time proportional to the gap between their smallest serial and the last card, then adds noise. Three skill levels: novice (large noise, slow to notice a hold: 80%), decent (middle: 90%), tuned (a practised team: 97%). Random is a player who lays at a random moment. 2,000 games per setting.

  • The success rate does not depend on how fast the group counts (all waits scale together), only on how much the players differ from each other. Game length does: at one serial point per second a climb takes about 40 to 60 seconds, so 5 to 8 climbs run about 5 to 8 minutes.

  • L1 (7 climbs, 1 card, players + 1 pawns): novice teams win 96%, 91%, 79% and 69% with 2, 3, 4 and 5 players; decent teams 99%, 98%, 96% and 94%. Random timing wins 58% at 2 players but 17% at 3 and under 2% at 4 and 5. Median length 6.6 to 7.8 min.

  • L2 (6 climbs, 2 cards): decent teams win 90%, 76%, 60% and 50% with 2 to 5 players; novice 76%, 40%, 19% and 7%; tuned 98%, 95%, 94% and 94%. Random never wins past 2 players. Median 6.4 to 7.3 min. Without the pawn win-back rule a decent team falls to 78%, 55%, 40% and 34%, so the win-back rule stays.

  • L3 (5 climbs, 3 cards, hold rule): decent teams win 82%, 62%, 43% and 30%; tuned 97%, 94%, 90% and 91%; novice 55%, 19%, 5% and 2%. Median 5 to 6 min. In 57% of two-player climbs, 75% of three-player and 91% of five-player climbs at least two neighbouring cards in the serial order share a team, so a hold comes up in most climbs.

  • Testing changed the team rule. The first version was "same team back to back costs a pawn" with no way out; its cost was set by the deal alone, and with 3 players, 4 pawns and 4 climbs it dropped decent teams from 43% without the rule to 10%. The hold, which lets a player who notices the team step aside safely, rewards noticing: a decent team (90% noticing) at L3 does a few points better than without the team rule at 3 players (62% against 55%).

  • Pawns were set at players + 1 for every level and climbs reduced to 7, 6 and 5 after a first try of 5, 4, 3 climbs ran only 3 to 5 minutes. Pawns players + 2 gave novice L1 teams 82% to 99%, and random timing 80% at 2 players, too easy, so L1 also uses players + 1.

  • Solo Ghost Climb (3,000 runs per setting): a bot that holds its cards until the gap is small ended with a mean of 2.0 slips at 3 cards, 2.9 at 4 and 3.9 at 5. Random choices got 2.2, 3.2, 4.2. The Lantern lowers it to 1.5, 2.3 and 3.3. The ghost cards are unseen so the solo game is mostly luck, and skill is worth under a slip.

Not tested:

  • Not tested: real timing. The tempo model is an assumption. Real children (and adults) can fall into a shared rhythm, which the model does not capture, so real success rates may be higher for practised groups.

  • Not tested: whether 5-year-olds read 2-digit serials and compare them under pressure.

  • Not tested: cheating by signals (breath, eye movements).

  • Not tested: solo ghost bots beyond a simple one that tries a single waiting threshold per run.

Rule card text

Text for the printed card (63.5 x 88.9 mm). Layout comes later.

Front

QUIET CLIMB. The mountain is silent. Climb it together. Pawns in the middle: one more than the players. Deal 1 card each (L1), 2 (L2) or 3 (L3). Find the serial: the small number in the pill. Without talking, lay your cards face up smallest first, all hands mixed. Someone lays a card while another holds a smaller one? Mistake. Show them, put them aside, lose a pawn. A perfect climb wins one pawn back. Win after the last climb with a pawn left.

Back

LEVELS. L1: 1 card, 7 climbs. L2: 2 cards, 6 climbs. L3: 3 cards, 5 climbs, plus HOLD: if your smallest card is on the same team as the card just laid (Team key, Ref 4), do not lay it. Lay your smaller held cards straight after the next card. MEDALS. Bronze: finish. Silver: finish with half your pawns. Gold: lose at most 1 pawn. SOLO: hold 3, 4 or 5 cards, row of ghost cards face down. Lay or flip. Count slips. Gold 1, Silver 2, Bronze 3 at L1.
