Expressions: 27 small stories

Each child has two cards and the two expressions are a pair: A in morning light and B at golden hour. The pair tells a tiny story (sneaking and then pouncing, sour and then bliss), so a game can ask you to act one out, match a face to its twin, or guess which card a clue describes. Behind the faces

Places in Bangalore

Every one of the 54 cards is set in a different place in and around Bangalore: a market, a temple, a fort, a lake, a hill. Here is where each one is, why it earned a card, and when and how to go. Visit all 54 and the deck becomes a bucket list.

Read this before you travel

Coordinates are approximate and come from general knowledge, not from a survey, so check the pin in Google Maps before you set out. 11 of the places are generic scenes on the card (an auto stand, a metro station, a coconut grove), and those are marked Representative pin: the pin is a good example of the scene, not a place the artist copied. Opening hours, fees and routes change, so confirm them before you go. Timings are suggestions for children and families.

Maps

Plotted from approximate coordinates on a plain grid with no streets. Select a dot to jump to its card. Places that sit close together overlap on the full-city map, so start with the central one. Colours follow the categories below.

All the places

Category
Light on the card

Auto-rickshaw stand outside Kempegowda Bus Station (Majestic)

Card K01 · Arvind, Monkeys · morning light

Everyday BangaloreMorningRepresentative pin

Why this place. The auto-rickshaw is the city's everyday ride, and Majestic is its busiest transport hub. This is a representative site for the card's morning scene, since the card shows a generic stand.

When to go. Weekday mornings are busiest and most photogenic, around 8 to 10 am. Any day of the year works. Keep an eye on bags in the crowd.

How to go. Namma Metro to Nadaprabhu Kempegowda Station Majestic (purple line) from MG Road, about 15 minutes. Most children enjoy a short metered auto ride; ask for the meter.

Open in Google Maps12.9776, 77.5727

Sankey Tank

Card K02 · Amay, Monkeys · morning light

Lake and parkMorning

Why this place. A man-made tank built in 1882 to bring drinking water to the city, now a favourite walking and picnic spot. The morning scene suits its boardwalk and tree-lined bund.

When to go. Early morning (6 to 9 am) for cool air and light, any weekday. Avoid the Ganesh immersion days in the monsoon season. Check current timings.

How to go. About 8 km north of MG Road, 25 to 40 minutes by taxi depending on traffic, or Namma Metro to Mantri Square Sampige Road then an auto. Limited roadside parking. Good for a stroller-friendly walk.

Open in Google Maps13.0072, 77.5732

Bamboo Avenue, Cubbon Park

Card K03 · Smaya, Bears · morning light

Lake and parkMorning

Why this place. Cubbon Park is the city's green lung, and the bamboo avenue is one of its quietest corners. It fits a card about shade and morning light.

When to go. Morning on a weekday, 7 to 10 am, when the park is cool and light filters through the bamboo. Vehicles are restricted on weekends, which makes it calm for children.

How to go. Walk from Cubbon Park or MG Road Metro stations (purple line), about 10 minutes. Parking is limited, so the Metro is easier. Flat paths, good for small walkers.

Open in Google Maps12.9752, 77.5948

Gavi Gangadhareshwara Temple

Card K04 · Nysha, Monkeys · morning light

Place of worshipMorning

Why this place. A rock-cut cave temple dating to the 16th century, famous for the sun's rays that light the Shiva lingam around Makar Sankranti in mid-January. It gives the deck its cave scene.

When to go. Visit on or around Makar Sankranti (about 14 January) for the sunlight alignment, in the late afternoon; the temple is crowded then. On ordinary days go in the morning and check current timings.

How to go. About 8 km south of MG Road, 25 to 35 minutes by taxi. Narrow streets and little parking, so use a taxi. Dress modestly and remove shoes at the entrance.

Open in Google Maps12.9438, 77.5636

Jawahar Bal Bhavan toy train, Cubbon Park

Card K05 · Idhayan, Monkeys · morning light

Everyday BangaloreMorning

Why this place. A small toy train runs inside Cubbon Park for children and has been a childhood treat for generations of Bangaloreans. It suits the youngest card in the deck.

When to go. Weekend and holiday mornings or late afternoons. The train usually does not run on all weekdays, so check current timings first.

How to go. Walk from Cubbon Park Metro (about 10 minutes) or MG Road Metro. Small ticket at the Bal Bhavan gate. Suitable for toddlers with an adult.

Open in Google Maps12.9779, 77.5944

Krishna Rajendra Market (City Market)

Card K06 · Anayka, Elephants · morning light

Food and marketMorning

Why this place. The city's oldest and largest wholesale flower, fruit and vegetable market, loud and colourful. It stands for the busy, working Bangalore.

When to go. Early morning, 5 to 9 am, when the flower trade is at its peak. Festival eves (Ugadi, Ganesh Chaturthi, Diwali) are the busiest and most vivid.

How to go. Namma Metro to KR Market Station (green line) from Majestic, about 10 minutes. Very crowded: keep children close and carry little. Better with older children.

Glass House, Lalbagh Botanical Garden

Card K07 · Dharsh, Elephants · morning light

ArchitectureMorning

Why this place. A 19th century iron and glass hall modelled on London's Crystal Palace, and the centre of Lalbagh's flower shows. It gives the deck a bright, light-filled morning scene.

When to go. Mornings, 7 to 10 am, on weekdays. The flower show runs around Republic Day and Independence Day; check current timings and entry fees.

How to go. About 6 km south of MG Road, 20 to 30 minutes by taxi, or Namma Metro to Lalbagh Station (green line) then walk. Park on the road outside the main gate. Wide paths suit strollers.

Attara Kacheri (Karnataka High Court heritage building)

Card K08 · Ajay, Cobras · morning light

ArchitectureMorning

Why this place. A red Greco-Roman building from 1868 that once housed 18 government departments and now houses the Karnataka High Court. Its colonnades give the card a stately scene.

When to go. Morning light on the red facade, a weekday or Sunday for a quiet view from outside. Courts are working on weekdays, so check what access is allowed.

How to go. Walk from Cubbon Park or Vidhana Soudha, about 10 minutes from MG Road Metro. It is best seen from the road, with no entry for sightseeing on working days.

Place of worshipGolden hour

Why this place. Malleshwaram's Sampige Road is lined with flower sellers and old shops near the 17th century Kadu Malleshwara temple. Rihansh's golden-hour card shows the street.

When to go. Mornings are lively with flower sellers; evenings have soft light. Festival days are very crowded. Dress modestly and check current temple timings.

How to go. About 8 km from MG Road. The Green Line to Sampige Road metro station is the easiest way; cab takes 25 to 35 minutes. Parking is limited. Keep children close in the narrow lanes.

Chickpet silk sari market

Card K54 · Gowri, Cobras · golden hour

Food and marketGolden hour

Why this place. Chickpet is the old textile market of Bengaluru, known for Mysore silk and sarees. Gowri's golden-hour card is set in a silk shop lane.

When to go. Visit on a weekday late morning or afternoon, as many shops close on Sundays and the lanes are packed at weekends. Festive weeks before Diwali are busiest. Check current shop timings.

How to go. About 6 km from MG Road. City Market and Majestic are the closest metro stations; cab takes 25 to 35 minutes. The lanes are crowded and parking is poor, so go by metro. Keep children close.
